{"description":"The shared server — not the session, and not a harness hook — keeps the working-tree export current after every graph change, coalescing bursts through a debounce, and sets the export's prev_content_hash from the export as committed on the default branch when a git repository is present.

WHY THE SERVER OWNS IT: the session is the thing that might not come back. The Stop hook fires once and exists in one harness, so a consumer of reflow2 in any other client would never see it.

WHY THE LINEAGE MOVES: continuous writing collides with one-export-per-PR only while the chain is built from the FILE on disk. Anchored at main, any number of commits on a branch each chain from main, and squash-and-merge lands exactly one hop per PR — which is what that rule always wanted. The "and it must be LAST" clause becomes automatic.

FOUR THINGS THE INCREMENT MUST STILL DECIDE, named on the rulings and deliberately not settled here: the debounce interval; the git query that finds main's version (merge-base survives a long-lived branch where head-of-default does not); the behaviour when the working tree holds a hand edit of the export; and the no-git fallback, which stays today's on-disk chaining so reflow2 assumes nothing about git.

AFFORDABILITY, MEASURED: a full export of the largest design in existence is 265 ms (2026-08-25, down from 1,168 ms), and the debounce means a burst of ten changes costs one export.","name":"The server writes the design export through to the working tree on every change, debounced, and chains its lineage from what is committed on main","provenance":"authored","status":"in_progress","tier":"operational"}
